Watts made this hymn from Psalm 141:2–5, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

2May my prayer be set before You like incense, my uplifted hands like the evening offering. 3Set a guard, O LORD, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips. 4Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing or take part in works of wickedness with men who do iniquity; let me not feast on their delicacies. 5Let the righteous man strike me; let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion. It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it. For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked. PSALM 141:2–5 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 141
Watch o'er my lips, and guard them, Lord, From every rash and heedless word; Nor let my feet incline to tread The guilty path where sinners lead. STANZA II
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 141. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
